headline: President Trump defended AI data centers at an Ohio rally for Senator Jon Husted, telling a muted crowd the facilities would otherwise go to China.
score_reason: The president makes data centers a campaign plank in a decisive Senate race, confirmed by AP and The Hill; held at the pool score since writers never raise one.
importance_line: Ohio voters worried about power bills, farmland and water now have the president arguing the other side in person, and Republicans must decide whether to follow him, while the one concrete measure, Husted's bill to charge big power users more, was blocked in the Senate this week.
summary: The Associated Press reports that President Trump, at a campaign rally in Vandalia, Ohio, on 3 Oct 2026 for Senator Jon Husted, defended the data centers that power AI, saying "you can't just turn them off, they'll go to China", and that his administration wants them to "benefit local communities"; AP noted the crowd, loud on other topics, went quiet on this one. Data centers have become the main line of attack by Democrat Sherrod Brown, who accuses Husted of handing "billions in tax breaks to Big Tech" as lieutenant governor, and Husted's own bill to make large power users pay more was blocked by Senate Democrats this week.
notes: AP original blocked (403); AP text read on Scripps News and cross-checked with The Hill. Follow-up of 1003:C05-01; new today is the Ohio rally.
